articles.title: Aston Villa sign Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis
articles.summary: Aston Villa complete the signings of Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris St-Germain and English centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton.
articles.body: Aston Villa have completed the signings of Senegal winger Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris St-Germain and English centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton.Mbaye, 18, arrives from Paris St-Germain for a fee of 55m euros (£47m), while Villa could pay up to £29m for Harwood-Bellis.Villa have paid an initial fee of £25m - with £4m in potential add-ons - for the 24-year-old defender after seeing two previous bids rejected.Mbaye scored three goals and provided two assists in 31 games in all competitions last season as PSG successfully defended their Ligue 1 and Champions League titles.The teenager appeared in all four of Senegal's matches at the 2026 World Cup, netting in a 3-1 defeat by France to become the youngest African player to score at a men's World Cup.Mbaye joined PSG in the summer of 2018 from FC Versailles 78, progressing through their youth academy and making his senior debut in August 2024 at the age of 16.The winger was born in France and represented Les Bleus at youth level, but switched international allegiance to Senegal in 2025 after qualifying through his father.A product of Manchester City's youth academy, Harwood-Bellis joined Southampton for £20m in 2024 after impressing on loan.A loan spell at Burnley in 2022-23 ended with a Championship winner's medal, before he helped Southampton to promotion via the play-offs in 2023-24.Southampton finished bottom of the table in Harwood-Bellis' first season as a Premier League defender, before they reached the Championship play-off final last season.However, Southampton were disqualified after the Spygate scandal and began the current campaign with a four-point deduction.Harwood-Bellis apologised for making a binoculars gesture during their play-off semi-final second leg victory over Middlesbrough.Mbaye is the latest attacker to join Unai Emery's side following Alejandro Garnacho, Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson.Harwood-Bellis replaces Ezri Konsa in Villa's defence, after the England centre-back made a £55m move to defending Premier League champions Arsenal.While Villa have spent around £280m over the summer, Unai Emery has lost several key members of his Europa League-winning squad.The club have raised over £313m in player sales, including Morgan Rogers' £117m move to Chelsea and Ollie Watkins joining Al-Hilal for £51m.Aston Villa have committed to spend about £280m in Emery's summer rebuild. The arrivals of Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis on deadline day shows Villa are continuing to spend big. They have broken their transfer record twice with the arrivals of forwards Johan Manzambi (£52m) and Nicolas Jackson (£65m) so cannot plead poverty.If all clauses and add-ons are triggered Villa would be pushing £300m this summer, despite needing to sell to comply with Uefa and Premier League financial rules. Uefa limits the amount of revenue spent on wages, transfers and agent fees to 70% and Villa have already breached the regulations twice. They were fined £19.4m in June - with £12.9m suspended - having been hit with a £9.5m sanction for a similar breach the year before and need to ensure they break even because of their settlement agreement with Uefa.Despite that, Matteo Ruggeri (£17m), Harwood-Bellis (£30m), Joao Gomes (£38m) Jackson, Zion Suzuki (£30m), Manzambi and Mbaye (£47m) have all arrived, while  midfielder Leon Goretzka has also joined on a free transfer after leaving Bayern Munich.That comes having brought in just over £300m through the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, Emi Martinez, Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins. That figure also includes the £10.3m departure to Benfica of Enzo Barrenechea, who never played a Villa game, and Roma paying £21.3m to make Donyell Malen's loan permanent.Emery said following Monday's defeat at Arsenal he was happy with their transfer business, and that everything Villa had planned for they had achieved.It was always going to be a summer of change at Villa Park, although the depth of the transition with so many key players leaving is something Emery has already admitted he did not expect.

articles.title: Noughties garage track named TikTok's UK song of the summer
articles.summary: Kyla's 2008 track Do You Mind gained worldwide recognition in 2016 when rapper Drake sampled it on One Dance.
articles.body: Noughties garage track named TikTok's UK song of the summerImage source, Northern Line RecordsImage caption, Kyla's 2008 track has featured in nearly 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summerByNaomi Clarke and Jordan KennyBBC NewsbeatBritish singer Kyla's Do You Mind has been named as TikTok's song of the summer in the UK after the noughties garage track experienced a resurgence on the app.The song gained popularity when it was first released in 2008, but it became known worldwide in 2016 when Canadian rapper Drake sampled it on his chart-topping single One Dance.It has now found a new audience by trending on TikTok, generating more than 500 million views from about 650,000 videos posted in the UK over the summer, according to the platform.Kyla, who created the song with her husband DJ Paleface, tells BBC Newsbeat it is "surreal" but "incredible" that Do You Mind is getting another moment nearly 20 years on.Image source, Northern Line RecordsImage caption, Kyla joined singer Jorja Smith on stage at All Points East festival last month to perform the track together"Back in 2016, even though it had all that success, it still felt like: 'Oh, it's because you're with Drake'," she says. "So you don't always feel validated."I think this time around it was like: 'Well this is actually me'."Singer Jorja Smith brought Kyla out on stage during her headline slot at All Points East festival in London last month to perform the track together.Kyla says hearing about 40,000 people sing the song back to her was an "incredible" experience which made her want to cry."It feels nice because it's mine. I'm happy," she says.The song has soundtracked a range of TikTok videos, from lip-syncs to outfit reveals.But Kyla says she personally loves the ones which play on the lyrics "baby" and "honey" by using dolls and real honey as props. Image source, Northern Line RecordsImage caption, Kyla's track became known worldwide in 2016 when rapper Drake sampled it on his chart-topping single One Dance'I'm hearing garage is back'UK garage music is experiencing a resurgence, with artists like Sammy Virji, AJ Tracey and Disclosure incorporating the sound into their work, while noughties girl group Mis-Teeq are reuniting. As part of the garage movement, Manchester-based artist Silva Bumpa's On 2nite has taken third place in the latest TikTok chart, and Prospa and Cloonee's Free Your Mind has made it to number seven. "I feel like a lot of people are saying funky house is back, then I'm hearing garage is back, but I do think it's a collection of people's tunes that they've really loved over time and they're just enjoying them again," Kyla says about the revival. "The younger generation are just learning these songs but they've been there for time." Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Katy Perry's The One That Got Away has been crowned TikTok's global song of the summerDo You Mind is not the only older song the platform has introduced to new audiences through trends this summer.Oasis' 1995 classic Wonderwall has secured the title of second biggest UK song of the summer on TikTok after becoming the unofficial soundtrack to England's World Cup journey. Its popularity in mass singalongs for fans prompted a 6,800% surge in searches for it since the start of the tournament, according to Tiktok. The track also featured in more than 300,000 videos and climbed back up the singles chart to number two. The continued love for the Britpop band also helped their track Champagne Supernova make it to number six in the TikTok top 10 list.The trend for nostalgic tracks appears to have been worldwide as US singer Katy Perry's The One That Got Away has been crowned TikTok's global song of the summer nearly 15 years after it was first released in 2011.It has featured in more than 15 million TikTok videos, with Perry saying it is "surreal" to see the track "having this moment all these years later"."From seeing it being chosen in the 'choose your own adventure' section of my Lifetimes Tour concert film to seeing people discover it on TikTok and make it part of their own stories has been really special to watch," she says. "It's nice to revisit an amazing chapter while watching another unfold."Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here.

articles.title: Ikea cuts prices as customers struggle with rising cost of living
articles.summary: The Swedish retailer has seen revenue decline as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to buy new furniture.
articles.body: Swedish furniture giant Ikea is cutting prices across hundreds of products in Europe to woo customers struggling with deepening cost-of-living pressures.Ikea has seen revenue decline over the past two years as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to invest in new furniture and home renovations.The company is spending €1.2bn (£1bn) on the price cuts to items including the Billy bookcase and Kallax storage units, with reductions of up to 28% on certain products.Ikea said it could make the cuts by making savings throughout the supply chain, such as packaging costs, but acknowledged profits may take a hit. Ingka, the franchisee which operates most of Ikea's European stores, said the cuts were "not an activity or short-term campaign"."It's about making IKEA more affordable when people need it most, even if it means accepting a lower margin," said Juvencio Maeztu, chief executive of Ingka. "The cost of living is increasing and it's getting tougher and tougher for many people."He added: "For many people, home is a bedroom in a shared house, and it's even more important to offer storage and organised solutions."Ikea has reduced its prices several times in recent years, even as it caused a hit to the company's revenue and profit in its most recent earnings report.

articles.title: Summer 2026 was UK's hottest on record, Met Office says
articles.summary: Met Office figures show that the previous record, set in 2025, has been broken after an unprecedented summer of persistent heat.
articles.body: In a rapid attribution study - which looks at how much of a role climate change plays - the Met Office say the average temperature was made around 130 times more likely due to human-induced climate change.And step back from this summer and there is clue to our changing climate in the temperature record itself.In a climate that isn't changing, new records should become progressively rarer, because every time a record falls, it raises the bar for the next one.Think about the 100m race.  Each time someone sets a new record, it becomes harder to beat.  And there's another thing.  Typically records are only ever broken by a few fractions of a second – often just a millisecond or two.In June 1991, for example, Leroy Burrell ran 9.90 seconds, beating Carl Lewis's 1988 world record of 9.92 seconds by just two hundredths of a second.Now look at the UK summer temperature record. Until last year, the four hottest summers on record were separated by just five hundredths of a degree.Then 2025 beat the previous record by 0.34C. And this summer has beaten that new record by another 0.40C.So after years when the record moved by tiny fractions, in just two summers the bar has been raised by 0.74C.Head of Climate Attribution at the Met Office, Dr Mark McCarthy said that summer 2026 was "remarkable" and we can expect to see extremes occurring more frequently in the future because of climate change.So why is this happening so quickly here? The UK sits on the western edge of Europe, the fastest-warming continent on Earth - warming at roughly twice the global rate.There are a few reasons for that. Land heats up faster than the oceans, parts of Europe stretch into the rapidly warming Arctic, and changes in weather patterns have favoured more frequent and intense summer heatwaves.Scientists are still working out exactly how much each factor contributes, but the result is clear: the background climate in which British weather happens is getting warmer.None of this means the UK will break its summer record every year. Weather will always give us cooler summers as well as hotter ones. But the pattern is becoming unmistakable: records that once marked the extreme edge of the UK's climate are being overtaken with remarkable speed.So the question is not whether the UK will experience summers hotter than this one. It is how often they will come - and how much hotter they might be.

articles.title: McTominay to miss Scotland games with minor heart issue
articles.summary: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay is to have a minor heart procedure after the discovery of "a mild benign arrhythmia", Napoli have announced.
articles.body: Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay is to have a minor heart procedure after the discovery of "a mild benign arrhythmia", Napoli have announced.The 29-year-old was subsituted after 56 minutes of Sunday's 2-1 Serie A defeat by Como and will have corrective treatment "in the coming days".Napoli expect him to return to playing after the international break in early October and McTominay himself posted on Instagram: "See you soon Napoli. I won't take long."However, it means he is likely to miss Sebastien Pocognoli's first four games as Scotland head coach, against Slovenia (home and away), North Macedonia and Switzerland in the Nations League.According to the NHS,, external an arrhythmia is when the heart beats too quickly or too slowly, or the heartbeat is not steady. Napoli say McTominay will undergo cardiac arrhythmia ablation - which the British Heart Foundation explains, external is when heat or cold energy is used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

articles.title: Laundry rooms to be turned into cells to tackle prison overcrowding
articles.summary: The government says £110m has been fast-tracked from existing budgets to speed up the building of new cells.
articles.body: The government is to create more cells in existing prisons in England and Wales as part of its plans to tackle overcrowding. An investment of £110m, which will come from existing budgets, will be used to convert unused office space, laundry rooms and storage space into cells, the Ministry of Justice said.Justice Secretary Alex Norris is also due to give more details in the Commons later on changes to the early release scheme, which aims to free up space in prisons as they near maximum capacity.He told the BBC prisoners being released early did not mean "freedom" and victims would have a say in restrictions placed on those criminals.Asked where clothes would be washed if laundry rooms were converted into cells, Norris told BBC Breakfast: "Of course we're going to make sure that the prisons can still function properly."This is a creative look, as I say, around our estate and being able to use some space that we can re-prioritise."Norris said he suspected the number of extra prison spaces created from freeing up existing space within prisons would be "landing somewhere in the middle" of 200 and 900.But Chairman of the Prison Officers' Association, Mark Fairhurst, said: "You can create as much additional space as you like, and build as many new prisons as you like, but where are the staff coming from to supervise people? Nobody wants to be a prison officer anymore."Norris said the government had delivered more than 3,200 prison places in two years.Investment on more prison spaces was announced in last year's spending review and the £110m is not new money, A £7bn capital investment plan to create 14,000 prison places by 2031. On the early release scheme for prisoners in England and Wales, Norris said victims were being sent letters informing them and offered support from victim liaison officers.He insisted offenders would face restrictions on their release, including tagging and bans on attending football games.Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman said victims wanted to know how these early releases would affect them, especially those who had faced domestic abuse or stalking.Plans for the early release scheme have been changed after concern about who would be freed.  Rapists, those found guilty of serious child sex offences and grooming offences were excluded. Then at the weekend Prime Minister Andy Burnham told BBC Breakfast anyone convicted of manslaughter would also now be excluded, following a campaign from PC Andrew Harper's family to block the release of two men convicted over his killing in 2019.Burnham said this would mean hundreds more prisoners staying in jail and extra prison space would be created by deporting foreign prisoners and releasing some inmates serving indefinite sentences.Among those no longer eligible for early release is Shane Kelk, who was jailed after a hit-and-run crash which left 20-year-old Amy Cooper dead.Amy's mother Amanda originally received letters telling her Kelk could be released early.She said the prospect made her feel "sick" and that it would have "devalued" her daughter's life.The block was a "massive relief", she said, adding that she was still "upset and angry" that she and other families had "been put through a period of uncertainty".Prisons in England and Wales are running at 97% capacity.Under the early release scheme some 4,500 prisoners are now expected to start being let out of prison in tranches from October.Government figures show there were 10,134 foreign nationals held in custody on 30 June, 3,283 of whom were on remand and would not be eligible for deportation.In the year to June, 5,962 foreign offenders were sent back to their home countries which is the highest rate of deportations since 2017, a 12% increase on the previous year.Plans to release prisoners still serving indefinite sentences under Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) have been criticised by the Conservatives, who say this in itself poses a risk of dangerous prisoners being released.IPPs have not been imposed since 2012 but there are still prisoners in jail in England and Wales who were given them.They were used where prisoners were considered to pose a significant risk of causing serious harm to the public. Once they had served a minimum term they could only be released if the Parole Board was satisfied they no longer posed a risk to the public. But ending indefinite sentences for those still serving them would require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

articles.title: What does Norris deal mean for Piastri? F1 Q&A
articles.summary: BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before the Italian Grand Prix.
articles.body: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli will try to tighten his grip on the drivers' championship on home ground at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix at Monza.However, the 20-year-old can expect to face a challenge from a resurgent McLaren and in particular Lando Norris, who has won the past two grands prix.And Monza is of course also home territory for Ferrari, although the long straights of the historic circuit may not suit the characteristics of their car.BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before round 13 of the 2026 season.What does Lando Norris' new contract extension mean for Oscar Piastri? There clearly is some tension behind the scenes and this season his development performance-wise has clearly dipped. - JuhaThere is no question that Oscar Piastri has not started this season as well as he did last.In 2025, the Australian for a large part of the year appeared on course for a first world title, until his season unravelled somewhat in the final third.This season, team-mate Lando Norris has won two races - and should have won a third in Miami.Piastri has only looked in contention for a victory in Japan, where he was leading and unlucky with the safety car, and Hungary, when Norris took his first win of the year.After taking the lead when Norris made an error on the first lap, there was some bad luck involved in Piastri losing the lead to Norris, when he was delayed lapping Carlos Sainz's Williams.But Piastri acknowledged it would have been difficult to hold Norris back if he had retained the lead because his pace on the hard tyres was weak. It became academic when he retired with a broken gearbox.Although the qualifying head-to-head statistics between them do not make pleasant reading for Piastri - Norris is 12-4 ahead - on actual pace, there is not a lot to choose between them over one lap. Norris is only faster by 0.071 seconds on average.It's fair to say, though, that Norris has been comfortably the more convincing race performer - hence the 55-point and three-place gap between them in the championshipThere seem to be a few things at issue here.One might be that Piastri has always been strong in high-speed corners. But the numbers of these that are grip-limited has reduced this year because the engines are often using them to charge the battery, something about which all drivers have complained. So that reduces a point of potential advantage for Piastri.Second, the cars have less downforce than last year, and Piastri is less comfortable than Norris in low-grip conditions.Finally, there is no question that Norris upped his game consistently over the course of the second half of last season to win the world title, and has continued to raise his level through this year. Without question, he is one of the drivers of the season so far.Team principal Andrea Stella said at the last race in the Netherlands: "Last year, we had seen already with Oscar that, from a technical driving point of view, when the car has this low level of grip, like we saw last year for instance in Mexico or in Austin, he needs to adapt the way he drives, the way he thinks, the driving, his expectations."This requires a bit of mental effort, which gets him to lose a couple of tenths of a second because you sort of have to process rather than drive through pure instinct because what happens is what you expect."So it's one of those cases in which you have to adapt your natural driving style to the demand of the car. So it stays in the space of driving and in the space of the technical side of things. I don't think it has anything to do with any psychological kind of opportunity. This is purely technical."Stella points out that the top three teams are very close in terms of performance, which means, as he puts it, "as soon as things are not optimised, then you may have a very significant positional loss - it's very brutal from this point of view".Both McLaren and Piastri reject any suggestion that there might be tension in their relationship.It's a fact, though, that McLaren wanted to sign Max Verstappen this summer, and that if they had it's virtually certain it would have been Piastri who was replaced.That possibility has receded for now, with Verstappen's new contract with Red Bull. But that contract has performance clauses, and if Red Bull are still struggling next year, it may well be that McLaren have another go for Verstappen.For now, Piastri is under contract to the end of 2027 at least, and will be focusing only on getting back to where he knows he can be.Why are Mercedes choosing to take a grid penalty for Kimi Antonelli at the next race in Italy? Why not take it at a future grand prix to give Kimi a better chance for a home win or is this not a concern for Mercedes? - MichaelMercedes have been quite open about the fact that Kimi Antonelli will take a new engine for the Italian Grand Prix, and with it a significant grid penalty that is likely to mean him starting at the back.The reality is that early season reliability meant this penalty - for exceeding the permitted number of engine parts - was inevitable, and Mercedes have calculated that Monza is the best place to take it for Antonelli.They have tried to make the decision on facts, and not let the emotion of it being his home grand prix enter into the equation.This decision will be based partly on the fact that Monza has long straights, and so is one of the tracks where a new engine and its slight performance increase will translate most effectively into lap time.But also important is Mercedes' analysis of how the engines in his 'pool' can be used most effectively over the remainder of the seasonTeam principal Toto Wolff said: "With Kimi, we are taking the full thing. In theory, our calculations say that it's the best track to take it. Obviously, algorithms don't take the nationality into consideration. I'm not ready to fight for a championship and get the best PR. That's what we're going to do."Antonelli's championship lead is still very comfortable, at 59 points. So he can afford to be phlegmatic about this.He says: "Of course, it's my home race and all that kind of stuff, but, you know, I think it's the best race to do so. So, I think it still will give me a chance to do a great result and bring home good points."George Russell will have to take a penalty soon, too. This is most likely to be at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, for similar reasons to Antonelli's being at Monza.Are Ferrari allowing emotion to get in their way? It's perhaps a stretch to say Ferrari can go on to win the title, but surely their best chance is backing the nearest challenger? Are they allowing the emotion of their attachment to Charles Leclerc, and his history with the team, to get in the way of making the clinical, ruthless decisions needed? - AlexPresumably this question is a reference to the brief dispute between Charles Leclerc and the team at the Dutch Grand Prix, when Lewis Hamilton was coming up behind him on fresher tyres mid-race.We dealt with what happened there in detail in last week's Q&A. But in the context of the question, it's worth pointing out that they actually did ask Leclerc to move out of the way to optimise Hamilton's race in Zandvoort.Ferrari operate a policy of equality between their drivers and only favour one over the other if it is obviously in the interests of the team.That could work either way, and the most obvious time it would be employed is if a race victory was at stake.Hamilton is their closest driver to the championship lead, at 59 points behind Antonelli. Leclerc is 28 points behind the seven-time champion - only four points further back than Lando Norris.Hamilton and Leclerc have won one race each, and the qualifying battle between them is incredibly close.Hamilton is ahead 9-7 on the head-to-head in races where a fair comparison can be made, but Leclerc is actually slightly quicker on average by 0.053secs.Beyond that, the question seems to presume that the team would favour Leclerc emotionally. But why make that presumption?Team principal Frederic Vasseur was instrumental in getting Hamilton to join Ferrari for 2025, but he has a long and close relationship going back many years with both drivers.Why would he be emotionally connected to one more than the other, or consciously allow emotions to rule his management decisions?Zandvoort is a great circuit and it's disappointing that they have pulled out of hosting the F1 grand prix for a second time. Is there any chance the circuit might return to the schedule some time in the future? - LynneIn F1, one quickly learns to never say never, but the chances of the Dutch Grand Prix returning to the calendar seem remote for the foreseeable future.The race was unique in that it owed its existence to the popularity of one driver - Max Verstappen.The organisers did an impressive job to host a grand prix at a track that has many logistical challenges, in terms of both its location and its facilities, and to make it work financially for as long as they did.It was highly popular with Dutch fans. But the event was privately run with no government financial support, and organisers decided that, as race fees went up, the risks that the event would not turn a profit were becoming too high.This decision was influenced by the fact that there had been a slight decrease in interest in the last couple of years. Understandable, as the novelty wore off. So organisers decided to end the event after a good run before any decline became more significant and they made a loss.F1 has no shortage of events with which to replace it. Portugal and Turkey are both coming back to the calendar next year, for example.

articles.title: Why did Modi urge Putin to end Ukraine war - and will he listen?
articles.summary: BBC correspondents in Delhi and Moscow look at why the Indian PM made a very public peace plea to his Russian ally.
articles.body: If anything, it is very much in line with India's policy of strategic autonomy. Which then begs the question: why would Modi say something on the war so publicly? The answer lies in the long-standing Russia-India ties - the two countries have generally found a way to work together, even when they see geopolitics through different lenses. Moscow has continued to be one of India's strongest allies despite Delhi forging closer relationships with Europe and the US in the past three decades.Delhi is one of the founding members of the Brics grouping of nations along with Russia and China, and it is also a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation with the two countries. But at the same time, Delhi is also a member of the Quad group with Australia, Japan and the US - Moscow has not been happy about this association.Still, Moscow and Delhi tend to work through these differences. Moreover, Russia still supplies around 40% of India's defence imports and it has also been a steady supplier of Delhi's energy needs.So, Modi's latest statement is not expected to cause any rift in Moscow-Delhi relations and analysts say it's unlikely that it would have come as a surprise to Putin or his diplomats. As for the West and Modi's critics in India, they will feel that the prime minister should have been even more direct in his criticism of the war.This isn't the first time a foreign leader has publicly urged Putin to end the war in Ukraine.Just five weeks ago the President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev suggested Putin freeze the conflict and return to the negotiating table.He didn't. And he hasn't.There's no sign of these public calls for peace changing Putin's calculations.To Modi's call for a cessation of hostilities, the Kremlin leader replied:"Thank you very much, prime minister. We are moving forward along this path."Polite, but vague. And non-committal.After all, a path can be short. But it can also be long. Very long.And "moving forward" at what pace?And, crucially, on which path?All the evidence suggests that Russia's leadership remains convinced it is on a path to military victory in Ukraine. To frame that in terms of peace, "moving forward" to peace on Russia's terms dictated by military success.Therefore, for now, the fighting goes on.Despite the fact that, after more than four-and-a-half years of war and huge military losses, the Kremlin has yet to secure victory.And despite Ukraine's success in bringing the war back home to Russians: for example, through long-range drone strikes on Russian oil refineries that have sparked fuel shortages and petrol queues across the country.

articles.title: Canada's Liberals sweep three seats in boost for Carney after trade tensions with US
articles.summary: One seat was taken from the Conservatives, indicating public support for the PM after a confrontation with Donald Trump.
articles.body: Mark Carney's Liberal Party won all three parliamentary special elections that were held in Canada on Monday, indicating ongoing public support for the prime minister well into his second year in office and after recent trade tensions with the US. The votes were triggered by the resignations of three MPs. The most notable result saw Carney's party claim a Québec seat previously held by an opposition Conservative.In the other two votes, in Ontario and British Columbia, the Liberals held onto their seats as pollsters expected.Carney has received a bump in the polls following his decision to end trade talks with the US, accusing Canada's southern neighbour of proposing terms that were "unfair".The prime minister congratulated the three victorious Liberal candidates in a post on X. Reflecting on the wider issues facing his premiership, he wrote: "Canada is being tested in a changing world, and Canadians are up for it."The results mean Carney will keep his slim majority in the House of Commons. Canadian media projected a sizeable victory for the Liberals in the Québec district of Chicoutimi-Le Fjord. Liberal candidate Daniel Gobeil, a dairy farmer, becomes the district's new MP, having claimed more than half of the overall vote.He beat the Bloc Québécois and the Conservatives into second and third places respectively. The seat had been a narrow three-way race last time round.Addressing his supporters in French, Gobeil said "this victory means we can maintain Canadian unity all across the country", CBC reported.Elsewhere, Tanveer Shahnawaz won his contest in Beaches-East York, Ontario, and Braeden Caley emerged victorious from the race in North Vancouver-Capilano, British Columbia.The Conservatives have struggled to close the gap with the Liberals since losing last year's federal election, with the latest polls suggesting they are trailing behind Carney's party by about 10 points. Four members of their ranks crossed the floor to the governing Liberals since the April 2025 election, and three others have either resigned or have announced plans to do so.Richard Martel, the former Conservative MP of the Quebec constituency that held Monday's by-election, stepped down last month after he was appointed by Carney to Canada's Senate. Senators in Canada are not elected. The loss of Martel's seat to the Liberals is another blow to Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre, who won a leadership test in January by a landslide but has faced questions about his ability to navigate the current political climate in Canada. Meanwhile, the approval of Carney's government rose four points in recent weeks, as has the prime minister's personal popularity, according to figures released on Monday by Canadian pollster Abacus Data, external.David Coletto, founder of Abacus Data, credits this boost to US President Donald Trump's lack of popularity with Canadians, as well as the country rallying around Carney's decision to walk away from trade talks with the White House. This trend is most pronounced in Quebec, Coletto wrote in a note on Monday, where "Carney's personal rating is stronger there than anywhere else in the country".Quebec stands to be one of the most provinces most affected by Trump's new 50% tariffs on a range of Canadian goods, which came into effect after trade talks collapsed earlier this month. In a recent report, global forecasting firm Oxford Economics warned that Quebec could lose C$2bn ($1.4bn; £1bn) in annual output by 2028.

articles.title: GB's Fery returns to Grand Slam stage - what lies ahead?
articles.summary: Shock Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery returns to the Grand Slam stage when he faces Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the US Open.
articles.body: During his time as a professional, Fery has always carried himself with an air of assurance.Although his extraordinary Wimbledon performance was unexpected, it feels he has the temperament to take the new experiences it has brought in his stride.His debut at ATP Masters level ended in a win over Australia's James Duckworth at the Cincinnati Open, although the speed and guile of world number eight Alex de Minaur proved too much in the next round.From there Fery travelled to North Carolina, where he finished runner-up at the ATP 250 event in Winston-Salem.While he lost to higher-ranked Peruvian Ignacio Buse in Saturday's final, Fery says his four victories - albeit against opponents a Grand Slam semi-finalist would be expected to beat - have enhanced his sense of belonging. "It was a very positive week for me. Obviously there is nowhere near as much attention as the Slams and big ATP events, but I've got to remind myself that its not a normal thing yet to make ATP 250 finals," Fery told BBC Sport. "I wasn't really happy with my match in the final, but it was a long week and first time I'd played five matches in five days in a very long time. "It's great preparation for the US Open."Fery narrowly missed out on a seeding at the US Open, which are given to the top 32 players, leaving him vulnerable to drawing one of the leading stars in New York.Musetti, who is an excellent returner and slick mover, must be counted among the title favourites in a wide open men's draw.A quarter-finalist in New York last year, the 25-year-old has gone a step further at both the French Open and Wimbledon in the recent seasons, and reached the Australian Open last eight in January.A thigh injury ruled him out of the French Open and Wimbledon, but he has showed signs of rediscovering his best level in recent runs to the Washington and Cincinnati quarter-finals."Some weeks you get good draws, some weeks you get tougher draws - it is how it is," said Fery."I missed out by one spot on a seeded position and then I draw the 13th seed - it's a bit unfortunate but some things go your way and some things don't. "I still feel I have my chances in that match-up if I prepare and play well."Whatever happens against Musetti, it will be intriguing to see how Fery fares over the coming months given his new-found status.There has already been plenty of discussion about whether the 5ft 9in Londoner's stature will be a limiting factor on an ATP Tour where taller players tend to thrive."I don't think Arthur's height has to be something which we sit here and worry about," says Michael Bourne, the Lawn Tennis Association's performance director."He has great ball speed – whether off the ground or from the serve, he's an amazing decision-maker and a very good athlete. "He's earned the right for us not to put a ceiling on him. He's a talented young man and there is a lot to be excited about - let's see how far he can go."

articles.title: Israeli fire kills three in Gaza City during reported raid, medics say
articles.summary: Unconfirmed local reports say the Israeli military carried out air and artillery strikes after a raid by an Israel-backed militia was discovered.
articles.body: At least two Palestinian children and a woman have been killed by Israeli fire in western Gaza City, Palestinian medics say.Unconfirmed local reports say that an Israel-backed Palestinian militia carried out a raid and that the Israeli military carried out shelling and air strikes after it was discovered.A third child was killed in a separate incident in central Gaza.Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said that a senior Hamas official had been arrested, but it is not clear whether the announcement is related to the incident in Gaza City.Videos from Gaza City captured chaotic scenes, with the sound of gunfire and the aftermath of air strikes.Initial Palestinian reports said that a special Israeli unit infiltrated a crowded area using a van and motorcycles.It is not clear whether those involved were Israeli forces or members of an Israel-backed Palestinian militia.A local source told the BBC that a senior Hamas security official was believed to have been targeted.The Israeli military reportedly carried out drone strikes to try to secure the special unit after its presence was uncovered.The military has only confirmed striking several targets in Gaza "in order to remove threats to the security forces", adding that there were no injuries to its troops.

articles.title: Man in court charged with murder after deaths of woman and girl in Teesside fire
articles.summary: A seven-year-old girl and her aunt died in the fire in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, on 26 August.
articles.body: A 23-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a woman and her seven-year-old niece who died in a house fire.Natalie McDonald, 34, died in the blaze in Grangetown, near Middlesbrough, in the early hours of 26 August, along with Valentina Foster.Jaden Wright appeared at Teesside Magistrates' Court charged with two counts of murder as well as multiple grievous bodily harm offences.Wright, of no fixed address, was remanded in custody during the hearing that lasted less than two minutes, and is next due to appear at Teesside Crown Court on Thursday.He is also accused of two counts of grievous bodily harm with intent and two charges of attempted grievous bodily harm with intent.These charges relate to the six people in the house at the time of the blaze.No pleas were entered during the hearing on Tuesday morning.

articles.title: Russian attack hits rail workers in new deadly strikes on Kyiv
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials say 20 people, including two children, were injured in the capital and the wider region.
articles.body: "Every day spent in war pushes humanity back, and every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm," Modi said at a security summit in Kyrgyzstan.Modi, whose country's economy depends heavily on discounted oil from Moscow, has made several similar pleas to Putin since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Overnight in Kyiv, eight people were killed and fires were reported in three city districts. Another four people were killed in the nearby town of Boryspil where a residential building was hit.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday morning that nearly 350 rescue workers had been working through the night in Kyiv and the surrounding region after the latest strikes.In a post on social media, he said Russia had fired a "significant number of jet drones and ballistic missiles". The strikes mark the sixth day of sustained Russian drone and missile attacks on Kyiv, in what appears to be a strategy aimed at exhausting Ukrainian air defences and undermining civilian morale.Russia's military warned over the weekend that its forces were preparing to carry out "massive" strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities.Eight other Ukrainian regions were attacked, Zelensky said, adding that an Indian national was among the casualties.Ukraine's Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivsky later said the Indian man - who turned 26 on Tuesday - was killed in Boryspil. The overnight attacks come after 38 people were killed in Russian strikes on a weapons depot in the Kyiv region on Friday, causing shells, mines and drones to detonate.Separately, a drone attack hit a major Russian Baltic Sea port in Ust-Luga, triggering a fire, Leningrad regional Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko said.Ukraine says targets like Ust-Luga - which handles millions of tons of petroleum products each year - are legitimate as they help finance Moscow's war effort.

articles.title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Andrew Bailey warns G20
articles.summary: The governor of the Bank of England warned of AI's “volatility” caused by energy shocks from the US-Iran war.
articles.body: The governor of the Bank of England has warned G20 finance ministers that artificial intelligence could cause a global economic downturn and pose a significant cyber security risk to financial systems.Andrew Bailey said any collapse of growth in the AI sector could lead to a "future market correction" that spreads worldwide.In an open letter to finance ministers in the US on Monday, he said companies around the world should prepare for security breaches "involving simultaneous disruption across multiple firms". Earlier this month, a group of 100 firms, including Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI, urged countries and groups to beef up their cyber defences before AI grows powerful enough to override them.Bailey told the G20 finance ministers that a combination of highly priced stock markets, increased borrowing by investors, and the growing concentration of money into a small number of major technology companies could amplify any future market correction."The issue is not simply that investors are borrowing more, but that leverage is interacting with high valuations and market concentration, in particular the increasing cross-investment between artificial intelligence (AI) companies and hyper scalers, in a way that could amplify a future market correction," he said.Bailey has called on those in charge of financial security to develop "appropriate steps to support safe and responsible model release and deployment on a global basis".Bailey, who was writing in his capacity as chairman of the Financial Stability Board international watchdog (FSB), expressed concern about the "volatility" prompted by the effect of energy supply shocks caused by the US-Iran war.His warning comes as the UK government is seeking to grow the country's "sovereign AI" capacity, developing homegrown AI technology to ensure the UK is not dependent on services from abroad.Ministers want to see companies compete for the funding to help tackle challenges like cutting waiting lists in the NHS and bolstering cybersecurity and defence.But there is growing concern that AI companies are increasingly developing models that can easily override the safeguarding systems of banks and financial centres.

articles.title: TP-Link’s first Wi-Fi 8 router is almost here
articles.summary:
Here you can see the Archer 8 Ultra (bottom) and the Deco 8 Ultra (top). | Image: TP-Link	

The Wi-Fi 8 standard is far from finalized, but TP-Link is almost ready to release its first hardware targeting the next-gen spec. It unveiled the Archer 8 Ultra tri-band router and Deco 8 Ultra mesh system at IFA 2026, which utilize the upcoming IEEE 802.11bn standard to "address the connectivity problems
articles.body:
The Wi-Fi 8 standard is far from finalized, but TP-Link is almost ready to release its first hardware targeting the next-gen spec. It unveiled the Archer 8 Ultra tri-band router and Deco 8 Ultra mesh system at IFA 2026, which utilize the upcoming IEEE 802.11bn standard to “address the connectivity problems people actually notice” instead of focusing on speed upgrades, according to TP-Link’s announcement.
The Archer 8 Ultra features 18 internal antennas, and can deliver wireless speeds of up to 19Gbps and 10Gbps over wired connection. The Deco 8 Ultra mesh system provides up to 22Gbps over wireless and 10Gbps wired connectivity, according to TP-Link, with a three-pack covering up to 9,800 square feet and supporting more than 200 connected devices.
TP-Link hasn’t revealed any prices, but says the Archer 8 Ultra will be available for preorder in “select regions” starting on September 30th. Availability for the Deco 8 is planned for sometime in Q1 2027, with other Wi-Fi 8 products — including range extenders, adapters, and the Roam 8 travel router — to follow in Q2 2027.
The Wi-Fi 7 standard was only finalized in January 2024, so these new products are set to arrive before many people have had the chance to upgrade to the previous specification. Wi-Fi 8 also isn’t expected to receive a finalized certification until May 2028. TP-Link clearly wants to get ahead of the competition, however, and soothe any concerns regarding how its next-gen products will be impacted by the US ban on foreign-made routers — while TP-Link’s Wi-Fi 8 products use Broadcom, Qualcomm, and MediaTek chipsets, it says it’s using “US-led hardware and software engineering to deliver the most reliable Wi-Fi ever built.”

articles.body:
Last updated: 2026-08-29; Google Ticket Number: #9-2777000041594
From Google: clarification on whether an IRS 501(c)(6) determination satisfies "tax exempt donations".
From readers: please share this post, especially to anyone at Google who may be able to help. Please do not contact Google support directly.
CautionSince 28 August, Google has rejected updates to AnkiDroid on the Play Store. Unless resolved, AnkiDroid will be removed from Google Play on 11 September worldwide (except for India and Russia).
AnkiDroid is a free, open-source flashcard app for Android with over 10 million installs, used worldwide for various purposes, primarily in medical education and language learning.
AnkiDroid's donations go to Open Source Collective, a US non-profit which acts as our fiscal host. It holds an IRS determination letter stating that it is tax-exempt under 501(c)(6). This determination letter has been provided to Google.
Google's payments policy states: "Other than the conditions described in Section 3 ..., apps may not lead users to a payment method other than Google Play's billing system"
Section 3 of the policy states Play billing "must not be used in cases where payments include … tax exempt donations".
Google's 2026-08-06 email states donations may only be collected for "a validated tax-exempt organization (for example, a validated 501(c)(3) charitable organization in the United States or the local equivalent)".
Google's 2026-08-07 email, [after receiving an IRS determination letter for 501(c)(6) status], states AnkiDroid "allows users to contribute donations to an organization that is not tax-exempt".
Google support's last reply is as follows:
As mentioned in the previous email, we reviewed the documentation you submitted but found that your app still violates the Payments policy.
Specifically, your app allows users to contribute donations to an organization that is not tax-exempt.
You can refer to the attached screenshot for additional information.
Google Support have not explained why a 501(c)(6) determination is insufficient.
Note501(c)(6) is a tax-exempt status; donations are not tax-deductible for the donor. Google's communications explicitly state "tax-exempt".
We are forced to remove donation links immediately from our Play Store build in 2.24.X, and are doing so under protest, as otherwise we would be unable to distribute AnkiDroid to the majority of our users who use the Play Store.
AnkiDroid is the Anki client for Android, developed and maintained by volunteers. Nothing is sold in the app and our Open Collective is the sole source of funding for maintenance and development. AnkiDroid is independent from Anki, AnkiWeb, AnkiMobile, and AnkiHub.
All funding goes to our Open Collective, where our ledger is public.
Open Source Collective - AnkiDroid's Fiscal Host
Open Collective: AnkiDroid - AnkiDroid's Public Ledger
AnkiDroid Open Source Team Developers
After reviewing your app, AnkiDroid Flashcards (package name com.ichi2.anki), we have found that it does not comply with one or more Google Play policies. Therefore, your app's status is affected. If you do not fix the issue by the following deadline, users in some countries/regions may not be able to use your app.

Submit your changes to Google for review. Go to [Publication Summary].

Also, in certain countries (such as India), you may be able to offer your app for a limited time without making changes by paying a specified service fee. You can also change the countries or regions where your app is distributed by following the steps in the Google Play Console Help Center article "Distributing your app release to specific countries."
For more information, please refer to the Payment Policies and Google Play Payment Policies pages in the Help Center. For more information about alternative billing options available in specific countries or regions, please refer to this FAQ.
If you believe Google's decision was incorrect, you can submit an appeal. It may take up to 7 days to receive a response (in exceptional cases, it may take longer).
Once you have completed fixing the issue, submit your app changes for review on the Google Play Console Publication Summary page.
For more information about the enforcement process, please refer to the Help Center article "Enforcement Process." For the latest information on Google Play policies, please see #PolicyBytes in the Android for Developers section. You can change the audio track in the settings to select your preferred language.

お客様のアプリ AnkiDroid Flashcards（パッケージ名 com.ichi2.anki）を審査した結果、Google Play の 1 つ以上のポリシーに準拠していないことが判明いたしました。このため、アプリのステータスが影響を受けています。ステータス: さらなる対応が必要以下の期日までに問題を修正していただけない場合、一部の国 / 地域のユーザーはお客様のアプリを利用できなくなる可能性があります。

非課税の対象となる組織への寄付である場合は、  非課税団体であることを証明できる資料（米国内の法人に対する Internal Revenue Service（IRS）の決定書）を、 再審査請求 ケースの作成 後に届くメールへの返信にてご提供ください。

アプリには国別の要件が適用される場合があります。また、  特定の国（インドなど）では、  所定のサービス料金を支払うことで、  変更を加えずにアプリを一定の期間提供できる場合があります。 Google Play Console ヘルプセンター記事「特定の国にアプリのリリースを配信する」 の  手順に沿って、 アプリを配信する国や地域を変更することもできます。
詳しくは、ヘルプセンターの お支払い に関するポリシー、および   Google Play のお支払いに関するポリシーについて のページをご参照ください。  特定の国や地域で利用できる代替の課金オプションについて詳しく  は、こちらの よくある質問 をご参照ください。
この問題の修正が完了しましたら、Google Play Console の 公開の概要 ページで、アプリの変更を審査のために送信してください。
違反措置の適用プロセスについて詳しくは、ヘルプセンター記事「違反措置の適用プロセス」をご参照ください。Google Play のポリシーに関する最新情報については、デベロッパー向け Android の #PolicyBytes をご覧ください。設定で音声トラックを変更すると、ご希望の言語をお選びいただけます。

articles.title: John Ternus is now the CEO of Apple
articles.summary:
Apple SVP John Ternus takes over as CEO from Tim Cook. | AFP via Getty Images	

For the first time since 2011, one of the world's most valuable companies has a new leader, as today marks John Ternus' first day as Apple's CEO. He's replacing Tim Cook, who will continue on as the executive chairman on Apple's board and departed with a letter to employees that remarked, "This place is proof that cult
articles.body:
For the first time since 2011, one of the world’s most valuable companies has a new leader, as today marks John Ternus’ first day as Apple’s CEO. He’s replacing Tim Cook, who will continue on as the executive chairman on Apple’s board and departed with a letter to employees that remarked, “This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters, and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it.”
Ternus is taking over a company dealing with the rise of AI, shortages of RAM and other components due to that growth in AI, and a political and economic situation that is only getting more complicated as time passes. He will also do it without many of the executives who worked with Cook and Steve Jobs, like Phil Schiller, who Bloomberg reported will step down from his role leading the App Store. 
Here’s a look at Apple’s senior leadership team as it stands today:
[Image: Here’s what Apple’s leadership team looked like under Tim Cook, and what it now looks like under John Ternus. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/Apple-leadership-before-after.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]
With Ternus in charge, Tim Cook has been moved to Executive Chair and Phil Schiller continues as an Apple Fellow, despite handing off his day-to-day tasks of heading up the Apple Store and Apple events. We can also see that Katherine Adams’ position of SVP of government affairs has been fully vacated, with some of that responsibility being handed to Jennifer Newstead and Tim Cook, who’s now Trump’s full-time handler. Apple’s former CFO Luca Maestri is no longer listed on the leadership team after he transitioned to the roll of VP of corporate services in 2024.
The first Apple hardware event of the Ternus era is just around the corner on September 9th, where we expect to see new iPhones including a foldable “Ultra.” It will give us an early glimpse of what to expect, and the new public faces of the company going forward.

articles.title: Shein valued at $26bn after long-awaited stock market debut
articles.summary: The firm's Hong Kong listing on Tuesday comes after a years-long quest to sell shares in New York and London.
articles.body: Ultra-fast-fashion brand Shein has been valued at $26.2bn (£19.3bn) after its first day of public trading, following a long quest to list on the stock market. The company was once estimated to be worth nearly $100bn, but has faced heated competition, trade tensions and questions over the ethics of its supply chain.Shein's share price fell in the early hours of trading but recovered ground before closing down just 0.12%.The company's attempts to list in the UK and US were scuppered after supply chain concerns and criticism of its environmental impact. On Monday, Shein priced its shares at HK$48.56 each, raising ‌13.6 billion Hong Kong dollars ($1.7bn; £1.3bn) from the listing.That gave the company a stock market valuation of $26.3bn.Shein's shares fell by as much as 10% in early trading before the losses eased. They closed at $48.50, leaving it valued at $26.15bn.Shein became hugely popular, especially among younger people, due to its ability to source the very latest fashions at ultra-low prices through a vast network of factories in China.At a ceremony to celebrate the listing, chief financial officer Leigh Gui said the company's model of selling large numbers of small orders with rapid payment options now reaches about 160 markets worldwide."Let global consumers enjoy the sound of fashion," he said after a gong was struck to mark the start of trading.Shein has more than 273 million active customers who placed a total of more than a billion orders in the year to the end of March 2026, the firm said in a filing ahead of the listing.But it now faces higher costs, regulatory scrutiny and more competition, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.For customers, the slump in Shein's shares is a sign that the firm's cheap prices are "becoming harder to sustain", which may lead to higher prices, she added.Founded in China and headquartered in Singapore since 2021, Shein has spent several years touting its credentials as a global company, but ultimately was forced to return to its Asian roots to go public.The company once looked set for one of the largest stock market debuts ever by a Chinese firm, with Wall Street in its sights.The firm's long road to the stock market highlights the geopolitical pressures and regulatory scrutiny faced by Chinese companies with global ambitions.Its business had surged during the Covid-19 pandemic as people, stuck at home, turned to online retailers. At the same time, social media influencers shared their hauls for millions of followers to see.Shein faced resistance from US lawmakers, who objected to the planned listing over concerns of forced labour in its factories. In response to such allegations, the company has said it takes a "zero-tolerance policy for forced labour".An initial public offering (IPO) in the US - by far Shein's largest market - would have offered it a chance to further increase its global profile and tap into Western financing.It has also been accused of copying other designers' ideas. Shein has said "it takes all claims of infringement seriously" and that it respects the rights of all designers.Shein also explored the possibility of making its stock market debut in London but faced similar opposition.The BBC has contacted Shein for further comment.

articles.title: Pakistan changes 'most shocking ever' - Afridi
articles.summary: Pakistan's decision to make dramatic changes to their squad during the series in England is the "most shocking decision ever", according to former captain Shahid Afridi.
articles.body: Five of the players dropped - Muhammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman and Khurram Shahzad - have featured in the series so far, while Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar have been sent home without playing.A total of seven players have been called up. Batters Saim Ayub and Abdullah Fazal have previous Test experience and join the quintet of uncapped newcomers.Spin-bowling all-rounder Arafat Minhas, left-arm seamer Mohammed Imran Jr, wicketkeeper Said Baig and all-rounders Mohammad Imran and Razaullah have all received call-ups.Ex-Pakistan captain Ramiz Raja, also a former chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I'm trying to convince myself this is all OK, but it is not."It just shows Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button."Pakistan are scheduled to have an audience with King Charles at Clarence House this week in an engagement that was planned before the series against England began.However, it is set to take place despite the series almost coming to controversial early end during the second Test.At lunch on the first day, the PCB threatened to cancel the remainder of the match and tour because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan that was broadcast by Sky.Imran, the former Pakistan captain and prime minster, has been in prison for three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.Pakistan ultimately completed the Test, with both captain Babar Azam and head coach Sarfaraz denying any knowledge of a planned boycott.

articles.title: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel?
articles.summary: The team behind Starcloud's orbital data centers has a new high-risk space project: Sending a probe to Alpha Centauri.
articles.body:
The founders behind Starcloud, a startup with plans to operate a fleet of GPUs in orbit, have a new pitch for potential investors: a plan to send a tiny spacecraft on an 80,000-year journey to Alpha Centauri.
If they do it, it will be the first human-built object explicitly aimed for another star, and the sixth to leave our solar system.
Dubbed Fermi Explorer, the non-profit behind the mission emerged today to ask for partners, donations, and advice. The initial team — Starcloud founders Philip Johnston, Adi Oltean, and Ezra Feilden, along with program manager Garret Jameson — has put together a plan to use proven space technologies to send a vehicle with a 10 cm square payload, weighing 1 kilogram, into interstellar space.
The founders say they are launching this mission in the spirit of human exploration; to achieve a historical first; and to test the limits of the Fermi paradox, which attempts to explain why we have yet to find other intelligent life in the universe and gives the mission its name.
The mission is intended to cost about $15 million and plans to launch in 2029. The non-profit is soliciting vendors to build the vehicle, funding to pay them, and scientific and artistic payloads to send, à la the sensors and Golden Record onboard NASA’s Voyager space probe, the first human spacecraft to leave our solar system.
Most plans for interstellar exploration stumble when dealing with the vast distances involved and the comparatively slow methods we have to cross them. Voyager, launched in 1977, is now about 26 billion km from Earth; Alpha Centauri, the nearest star to our solar system, is 41 trillion km away.
The last time Silicon Valley took on this challenge, a non-profit called Breakthrough Starshot, founded in 2016 by Yuri Milner and backed by Mark Zuckerberg, envisioned a multibillion-dollar effort to use a novel laser-based propulsion system to reach Alpha Centauri in 20 to 30 years. The effort collapsed in 2025, but the dream apparently remains alive.
Fermi Explorer takes the opposite tack: Rather than pushing the frontier of technology, the goal is to use what we have already to do something.
“I also got excited and then disappointed!” Johnston said of Starshot. “That’s the reason we are doing the mission. We are hell-bent on actually launching something in three years … The big difference with most other [interstellar] missions and the Fermi Explorer is that the others all try to do it in a human lifetime, which means billion-dollar propulsion R&D programs. We have very deliberately picked 80,000 years as the minimum viable mission.”
The plan is to launch the spacecraft on a rocket rideshare, then use efficient but low-power electric propulsion to slingshot the vehicle into a series of orbits that will eventually leave it bound for Alpha Centauri. The spacecraft is intended to be active for about 12 years before entering a final coast phase toward the other solar system.
“If a dinosaur bone can last 200 million years, then a metal box can easily survive the radiation environment we expect for 50,000 years,” Johnston said. “We don’t plan on powering spacecraft up at the end of the 80,000 years. We hope that a future human civilization will intercept it.”
When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn’t affect our editorial independence.
Tim Fernholz is a journalist who writes about technology, finance and public policy. He has closely covered the rise of the private space industry and is the author of  Rocket Billionaires: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos and the New Space Race. Formerly, he was a senior reporter at Quartz, the global business news site, for more than a decade, and began his career as a political reporter in Washington, D.C.
You can contact or verify outreach from Tim by emailing tim.fernholz@techcrunch.com or via an encrypted message to tim_fernholz.21 on Signal.
